annotations.text:
The problem isn't the engine — it's that the build reads like a settings menu.

Same information, restyled so it reads as a game: a glowing Altar as the hero, chunky tactile shards you want to press, one obvious action.

This screen is the growth engine — the moment players screenshot and post.

The odds line ('1 in 12,400') is the bit that makes a rare drop worth sharing. Currently the game shows a small grey card here.
Grid, not a list. Collection games live on the wall-of-things-I-own feeling, and locked slots showing their rarity are what pull players back to fuse again.

Two alternates to the dark 'Arcane Workshop' direction, in case that read isn't right. B is bright and friendly (skews younger, matches the big farming sims). C is neon arcade (skews older/teen). Pick one and I'll build it out properly.
